transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-01
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Lena Morales (Redwood AE), Devon Park (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (Redwood CSM); Marcus Lee, Sofia Alvarez, Tom Reynolds, Aisha Khan (Halcyon)
Links shared: onboarding-runbook.redwood.link, security-pack.redwood.link, perf-benchmark-template.xlsx

Summary: Quick kickoff & security intake for Halcyon Retail's implementation. Confirmed networking constraints, SOC2 evidence request, pilot scope (cart personalization model serving), and next steps around provisioning a short Dedicated trial for latency benchmarking.

[00:00] Lena Morales: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really appreciate you blocking time. I'm Lena, AE on the account, and we also have Devon, our solutions engineer, and Priya from CSM. How's everyone doing?

[00:10] Marcus Lee: Good, thanks. Busy week but ready to get moving.

[00:15] Sofia Alvarez: Yep, hi all. Excited — we've got a tight timeline so we want to align on security and perf up front.

[00:23] Lena: Totally. Quick agenda — go over Halcyon's goals for the pilot, networking and security checklist, propose a recommended infra for runway (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private), and agree on next steps. Feel free to interrupt.

[00:36] Tom Reynolds: One ask from security: we need proof of SOC2, ISO27001 certs, and details on key management—like can we bring our own KMS? Also data residency for logs.

[00:47] Priya Singh: Yes, we've got a security pack, I can share that immediately; it includes SOC2 type II attestation, encryption in transit and rest details, and KMS integration patterns. We'll also include an example audit log export.

[00:58] Aisha Khan: Great. On networking, our infra team wants to see exact egress IPs or a clear VPC peering flow. We're on AWS in us-west-2.

[01:10] Devon Park: For VPC/private deployments we support customer-managed VPC with a private control plane — you can bring your KMS and we can integrate via IAM roles. For the Dedicated trial we'll provide a small GPU pool inside a customer VPC or peered VPC depending on your preference.

[01:28] Marcus: We prefer peering so we can control routing policies on our side. Latency SLO is important — sub 120ms p95 for single-turn personalization in prod is our target.

[01:40] Devon: Understood. For sub-120ms p95 we usually recommend Dedicated with optimized kernels and quantization where acceptable. Hosted can hit decent latency but depends on concurrency — Dedicated gives predictability for the pilot.

[01:58] Sofia: We have a constraint: some of our data can't leave region and logs must sit in our account. Can Redwood support logging to a customer S3 bucket or streaming to our Splunk?

[02:12] Priya: We can stream audit logs via Kinesis/S3; we'll include the pattern in the runbook. Also we support retention policies per route.

[02:25] Tom: How about model artifacts — will model files be stored in Redwood's account? We want to bring our own fine-tuned checkpoint and keep it in our S3.

[02:36] Devon: Yes, you can host artifacts in your S3 and we support loading models from a pre-signed URL or via an integrated role. We'll document the exact steps. There was a note that artifact distribution for Dedicated can be done through private registry syncs.

[02:51] Marcus: Pricing-wise, we're evaluating cost vs latency. If we go Dedicated for the pilot and then scale, how do burst charges or autoscale work?

[03:03] Lena: Good question. For Dedicated we have reserved pools and burst options. We'll send a pricing sheet but high level — Reserved commit for baseline, with burst capacity charged per GPU-hour. We can model a projected monthly based on your QPS and average token lengths.

[03:20] Sofia: Also curious about batching — our personalization flows are short prompts (40-80 tokens) but high QPS. Would batching be recommended?

[03:30] Devon: Continuous batching helps a lot for cost, but it trades off latency. For short prompts at high QPS, small-time-window batching combined with KV caching for prefixes can reduce token cost without violating your latency SLO. We'll run a small experiment on the trial cluster to tune batch windows.

[03:52] Tom: Security deep dive: do you support customer-managed KMS keys (AWS KMS) and HSM-based signing? We need key rotation policies and audit trails.

[04:05] Priya: We support BYOK via KMS metadata; rotation is manageable through your KMS policies. For HSM-level requirements we have an enterprise option; I'll flag that to our security team to follow up.

[04:20] Marcus: Timeline: We want the pilot running in 3 weeks — is that feasible?

[04:25] Lena: It's ambitious but doable. Typical flow: security intake + networking (1 week), Dedicated provisioning + model load + basic perf testing (1 week), customer validation (1 week). We'll prioritize security docs and CIDR so provisioning can start.

[04:39] Aisha: We'll need a checklist. Who owns the networking config? Halcyon will provide CIDR and allowed IPs, Redwood will provide firewall rules and peering steps?

[04:48] Devon: Exactly. We'll provide a Terraform snippet and the VPC peering info. We also can support an IP allowlist if you prefer egress through a NAT with fixed IPs.

[05:01] Sofia: On the model side, our baseline is a 7B open decoder model fine-tuned for ranking. We plan to ship a quantized int8 variant for production. Any gotchas we should know about?

[05:14] Devon: Int8 is generally good but watch for small-quality regressions versus fp16; we'll run quality evals tied to your prompt set. Also some runtime optimizations require compatibility with the model architecture—if there's custom ops we'll need to test.

[05:32] Marcus: Do you have a recommended eval harness? We have test prompts and golden outputs for personalization; want to avoid regressions.

[05:40] Priya: We have an eval runner that can run your prompt set against model variants and produce a quality delta report. We'll ask for a representative prompt set (maybe 500 examples).

[05:51] Tom: Back to audit logs — retention policy on Redwood's side? We need 1 year of full audit logs, and alerts for failed auth attempts.

[06:03] Priya: We can configure retention; for enterprise accounts we support longer retention and alerting hooks into your SIEM. I'll include the options in the security pack.

[06:15] Marcus: Great. Let's talk concrete next steps and owners.

[06:20] Lena: Sure — I'll share the onboarding runbook and network diagram today, plus the SOC2 pack. Devon will own the perf run and send a benchmark plan. Tom, Halcyon will provide KMS ARN and CIDR by next Monday. Anything else?

[06:36] Aisha: We'll need to sync calendar for the deep technical session — prefer early next week.

[06:42] Devon: I'll propose 60-90 minute slot for the deep dive where we can run through perf knobs, quantization tradeoffs, and the benchmark template.

[06:52] Sofia: One more question — can Redwood integrate with our feature store for contextual signals? We plan to pass user embeddings and features in requests.

[07:01] Devon: You can pass structured inputs with feature vectors; we support function-like structured payloads and will recommend field limits to keep token overhead reasonable. Also suggest caching stable user-level context in the KV layer.

[07:20] Marcus: Ok. On the pilot success criteria — we want: 1) p95 latency <120ms on pilot traffic, 2) model quality within 2% of current baseline on eval, and 3) audit/logs integrated with our SIEM.

[07:36] Priya: Noted. We'll align the runbook to those criteria and include measurement dashboards.

[07:44] Tom: Any blockers from Redwood's side?

[07:47] Lena: No blockers — we'll need your CIDR and KMS info to start provisioning. We'll also ask for the 500-example eval set and a sample of typical prompts for latency testing.

[08:00] Aisha: We'll get that over by end of day Monday.

[08:05] Lena: Awesome. I'll follow up in email with links to the runbook and a short checklist. We'll also open a joint ticket and add Devon and Tom as technical points of contact.

[08:17] Devon: Quick note — for the Dedicated trial I'll set up one small GPU pool (2 x A10 equivalent), attach a small concurrency cap, and run the baseline workload. If we see tail latency spikes we'll iterate on batch windows and KV caching.

[08:34] Marcus: Sounds good. On billing — is the trial covered? We want to ensure no surprise charges.

[08:40] Lena: Trials are covered by Redwood for initial benchmarking; any extended reserved capacity would be a separate contract. We'll document limits in the trial agreement.

[08:52] Sofia: Anything else?

[08:55] Priya: I'll capture action items and send the security pack and runbook. Devon will post the benchmark template. Lena will send pricing/trial terms.

[09:05] Tom: Thanks everyone.

[09:08] Lena: Great, thanks all. Recap in the doc: Redwood sends runbook, security pack; Halcyon sends CIDR, KMS ARN, eval prompt set; schedule deep dive for week of Apr 6. We'll reconvene after the perf test.

[09:20] (meeting ended)

Notes on transcript quality: automatic transcription with occasional mis-heard technical terms (e.g., "KV cache" rendered correctly most places; "Redwood Dedicated" sometimes heard as "Redwood dedicate"), some overlapping speech not fully captured.
